claims.text: The starting AlCrFeNiSi powder has a tailored particle-size distribution and near-optimal spherical morphology suitable for LPBF.
AlCrFeNiSi miniature components can be fabricated by room-temperature 3D ink extrusion followed by sintering below 800°C in an inert atmosphere.
The proposed process applies to components with dimensions of 1–10 mm and layer thicknesses of 20–100 µm.
Residual stress and mechanical properties will be evaluated by X-ray diffraction and tensile or compression testing at room and moderately elevated temperatures.
Room-temperature ink deposition produces lower thermal gradients than LPBF deposition.
Reduced deposition thermal gradients minimize rapid-solidification defects.
Reduced deposition thermal gradients produce a more homogeneous microstructure with fewer microcracks and lower residual stress.
Sintering below 800°C can consolidate the ink-extruded build without reintroducing a significant thermal load.
Avoiding the rapid melt-solidification cycle of LPBF minimizes thermal shock and associated microstructural defects.
Low-temperature sintering ensures consolidation while maintaining a refined microstructure.
The proposed mechanism enhances both strength and ductility relative to LPBF.
Ink-extruded and sintered AlCrFeNiSi parts will have lower residual stress than conventionally LPBF-produced parts.
Ink-extruded and sintered AlCrFeNiSi parts will contain fewer microstructural defects than conventionally LPBF-produced parts.
Ink-extruded and sintered AlCrFeNiSi parts will exhibit a superior strength-ductility balance relative to conventionally LPBF-produced parts.
Conventional LPBF typically produces high residual thermal stresses and compromised mechanical properties because of rapid melt dynamics.
Conventional LPBF has complex processing requirements.
The proposed benefits may diminish when the sintering temperature exceeds approximately 800°C.
Ink formulations that cause incomplete consolidation may diminish the proposed benefits.
The benefits may vary with miniature-component feature resolution.
The magnitude of residual-stress and mechanical-property improvement depends on ink formulation, sintering kinetics, and environmental controls.
